newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU starts probe into Infraleuna aid.
newsitem.headline: EU starts probe into Infraleuna aid.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednedsay it had started a probe into financial aid amounting to 532.5 million Europan currency units in favour of Infraleuna Infrastrukur- und Service GmBH.
The former East German company supplies services to chemical companies in the eastern city of Leuna.

The Commission said in a statement it had "serious doubts" about whether the aid could be allowed under European Union laws, saying it was concerned that the amount could rise above that allowed for former East German companies.
Thirty-five percent of investment in large privatised companies in former East Germany can be in state aid under an EU exemption for the region.
Leuna is jointly owned by Germany's Linde AG and Belgium's Domo Group, with 49 percent in the public sector.
The German privatisation agency BvS set up Infraleuna to manage services for the chemical complexes in Leuna. It had no comment on the Commission's decision. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
